chase_cards.name: Lucky Stadium [Onix] [Kyūshū]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because Lucky Stadium is not one card here; it is a map. The Kyūshū print makes tournament participation, a region, a landmark, and Onix's stone-body presence all count inside one Stadium card.

key_artists.name: Ryuta Kusumi and Benimaru Itoh
key_artists.why: This credit matters because the card is not simply character art. It is cartography, event memory, and mascot placement: Onix has to belong to a specific regional stage, not just appear on a Trainer card.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Kyūshū World Challenge Summer participation-prize source group as one row containing Lucky Stadium at source index 166.

Bulbapedia says Lucky Stadium was first awarded to participants of the Japanese World Challenge Summer tournaments held between July and August 2000, with eight variations printed, each exclusive to a region of Japan.
Bulbapedia lists the Kyūshū print, featuring Onix, as available at the West Japan General Exhibition Center in Fukuoka on July 30, 2000.
PokeBoon identifies Lucky Stadium [Onix] [Kyūshū] as a World Challenge Summer participation prize and gives the same Kyūshū / Onix identity.
Bulbapedia's Lucky Stadium gallery credits the Kyūshū region print to Ryuta Kusumi and Benimaru Itoh.
PokeBoon also credits Lucky Stadium [Onix] [Kyūshū] to Benimaru Itoh and Ryuta Kusumi.
Bulbapedia says all World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium prints feature regional landmarks; the Kyūshū print features Mount Aso, Japan's largest active volcano.

Bulbapedia separates the regional World Challenge Summer prints from the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print, Neo Destiny English print, Intro Pack Neo print, and Pokemon Center New York print, each of which has different artwork or route.

As judged collector texture, the Kyūshū print matters because it turns a tournament participation card into a regional postcard: Onix, Mount Aso, Fukuoka, and the World Challenge Summer route are all part of the card's identity.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Onix] [Kyūshū]: a tournament card as a map
narrative.why_it_matters: The World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium cards are wonderful because they make a card behave like a place. Kyūshū is not just a parenthetical label here: the Onix, Mount Aso, Fukuoka event route, and regional tournament memory are all load-bearing. It is the kind of promo where a collector is not only asking whether they have Lucky Stadium, but which piece of the 2000 Japan map they are holding.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A seller, collector, or agent identifies a Lucky Stadium as the World Challenge Summer Kyūshū participation-prize print.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Do not identify this row from Lucky Stadium name alone. The legible target is the Kyūshū regional participation prize: Onix + Kyūshū route + Mount Aso / Fukuoka event context.
steps: Confirm the card is a Japanese World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium regional print, not the English Neo Destiny 100/105 card.
Confirm the featured Pokemon is Onix; other regional World Challenge Summer prints feature Lugia, Ho-Oh, Gyarados, Zapdos, Diglett, Mew, or Pikachu.
Ask for clear front images of the regional artwork and any readable event/region text; Kyūshū should not be inferred from Lucky Stadium name alone.
Screen against the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual Lucky Stadium, Intro Pack Neo Lucky Stadium, Pokemon Center New York Lucky Stadium, and later Stadium cards before publishing a confident row match.
If a seller calls it 'Kyushu Lucky Stadium' but shows no Onix/region evidence, mark the identification provisional and ask for targeted photos.
Do not promote regional identity into authenticity, possession, condition, or price truth.

card_profile.identity: Lucky Stadium [Onix] [Kyūshū], World Challenge Summer participation-prize regional Stadium card

claims.text: The local catalog anchors row 166 as Lucky Stadium in the World Challenge Summer Kyūshū participation-prize source group, with Onix as the row's distinguishing Pokemon signal.
Bulbapedia identifies Lucky Stadium as a Stadium card and lists the Japanese name as ラッキースタジアム Lucky Stadium.
Bulbapedia's card text for the Neo Destiny-style Lucky Stadium effect lets each player flip a coin once during their turn before attacking; on heads, that player draws a card.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon both associate the Kyūshū Onix Lucky Stadium artwork with Ryuta Kusumi and Benimaru Itoh.
As judged art texture, the Kyūshū card works because Onix is not decoration; its stone-body identity rhymes with Mount Aso and makes the regional landmark feel like part of the Pokemon world.

The Kyūshū print is one member of an eight-print World Challenge Summer regional set; Bulbapedia lists separate region/Pokemon pairings for Kantō/Lugia, Kansai/Ho-Oh, Hokkaidō/Pikachu, Chūbu/Zapdos, Hokushin'etsu/Mew, Chūgoku-Shikoku/Gyarados, and Tōhoku/Diglett.

As judged collector texture, Lucky Stadium [Onix] [Kyūshū] is the kind of card that rewards set-building discipline: the name is shared, the rules text is shared, but the region/Pokemon/artwork assembly is the collectible object.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Onix] [Kyūshū]: holding one region of a map
narrative.why_it_matters: This card asks the collector to slow down. Lucky Stadium is not enough. Onix is not enough. The Kyūshū print is the particular assembly: regional tournament, Fukuoka stop, Mount Aso landmark, Onix as stone-bodied mascot, and the shared Stadium mechanic underneath it. That is exactly the kind of object an agent should keep crisp: same title, different place, different memory.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A card-level Lucky Stadium match is being prepared for a want, sale, dossier, or agent comparison.
special_identification_instructions.summary: The card name is too broad. Confirm the Kyūshū regional print by Onix, regional/event cues, and exclusion of the other Lucky Stadium routes.
steps: Confirm the front artwork features Onix; this is the Kyūshū print's key Pokemon cue.
Ask for close images of any region/event text and the whole artwork field; do not infer Kyūshū from a seller title alone.
Compare against all other World Challenge Summer regional prints: Lugia, Ho-Oh, Gyarados, Zapdos, Diglett, Mew, and Pikachu variants.
Compare against the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual Lucky Stadium and ordinary Neo Destiny / Intro Pack Neo / New York City Lucky Stadium prints.
If the user provides only a cropped card title or a generic Lucky Stadium listing, mark the row match provisional and request full-front evidence.
Do not treat CGC/PSA population, auction title, or marketplace category as physical-card proof without matching images and seller evidence.
